football_evidence.question: Can Texas State win at the line of scrimmage?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Texas State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 4.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Texas State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Texas State’s offense averages 9.5 yards per pass attempt, and Boise State’s defense allows 8.9 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
When Texas State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Texas State’s offense averages 6.5 yards per carry, and Boise State’s defense allows 5.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Texas State has the ball (big plays through the air): Texas State’s offense turns 15.1% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Boise State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 12.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When Texas State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Texas State’s offense turns 9.4% of its runs into explosive gains, and Boise State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
contradicting: When Boise State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Boise State’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.6% of its dropbacks, and Texas State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Texas State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Texas State’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.7% of its dropbacks, and Boise State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 12.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Texas State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Texas State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 12.0% of its runs, and Boise State’s defense stops 26.1% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
In his last two games (Colorado State and Utah State), Jackson averaged 6.7 yards per attempt, against 8.9 in his five games before that.
quarterbacks: Maddux Madsen has completed 124 of 190 passes (65.3%) for 1,445 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and no interceptions in seven games for Boise State, and has been sacked on 5 of 195 dropbacks.

Brad Jackson has completed 133 of 195 passes (68.2%) for 1,606 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in seven games for Texas State, and has been sacked on 8 of 203 dropbacks.
